subject: docs/coop/artifacts/doctor-actor-join-integration-contract.v2.json

shouldFix.title: The repaired fixture's exact host-outside-DR-105 roster contradicts the carried D-032 treatment of doctor's default reads and operational-metadata write
evidence: FC-JOIN-HOST-OUTSIDE-DR105 now says host-side attempts outside DR-105 are exactly the CA-1 SPAWN decision, CA-1 IN_PROCESS attempt, CA-2, CA-3, and CA-4-HOST.

The same candidate carries adopted D-032 verbatim and extracts BLK-6 as DISCHARGED-AS-INAPPLICABLE for host default reads and doctor's operational-metadata write, expressly stating that FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE is not a component grant. Both recorded host-effect generations repeat that BLK-6 disposition.

The exact roster is therefore false unless it is explicitly scoped to the four doctor consent action classes. As written, it excludes two host-under-instruction effect families that the governing decision places outside DR-105, and no separately named fixture class tests their actor boundary.

The artifact applies nothing and its fixture classes are NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED, so the overclosure has not yet authorized or executed an unsafe path. That bounds this defect to SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: A future fixture corpus can treat doctor's default reads or operational-metadata write as a DR-105 component request, or omit the fail-closed behavior for a denied host state class, while still claiming conformance to the candidate's supposedly exact host actor matrix.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Scope the exact list to consentable CA-1..CA-4 host attempts and name a separate join fixture for D-032's host default reads and doctor's operational-metadata write. That fixture must state that these are not DR-105 component grants and must preserve fail-closed behavior when the applicable host class is denied. Do not mint a permission token or reopen BLK-6.

shouldFix.title: The matrix is phase-exact only for CA-1: it omits the CA-2 customer-tool tail and types component egress as CA-4 instead of the recorded PT-NET-EGRESS route
evidence: Doctor v4 CA-2 says a customer-owned tool is outside OpenSIP's signed closure and doctor cannot state what it reads, writes, or sends. Both host-effect v8 and v25 split that phase: the CA-2 process-creation decision is the host act, but the tool's subsequent effects are unbounded; its sockets are neither component PT-NET-EGRESS nor authorized by host CA-4, and every CA-2 execution remains unexercisable in the architecture preview.

Both named permission generations contain the contrary inherited PT-NET-EGRESS recital that component-originated egress includes a process doctor spawned under CA-1/CA-2. The candidate names those permission candidates and both host-effect generations but never mentions customer tools or PT-NET-EGRESS, so it neither exposes nor routes this live recorded-input conflict.

The repaired component-tail text repeatedly calls a spawned admitted component's network effect 'component-originated CA-4 egress'. Doctor v4 defines CA-4 as any network send or receive by doctor, while both host-effect generations define CA-4-HOST as the doctor process's own network effect and expressly route component-originated egress exclusively to DR-105 / PT-NET-EGRESS. The D-032 phrase 'component CA-4 egress' therefore needs a typed disambiguation before it becomes a fixture class.
A byte search of the candidate finds zero occurrences of PT-NET-EGRESS, customer tool, or customer-owned tool, despite claiming a phase-exact actor matrix over these named inputs.

CA-2 is still denied, no candidate is applied, and no fixture is authored or executed, so this unresolved join does not presently grant an effect. That bounds the defect to SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: A future fixture author can serialize component egress as doctor actionClass CA-4, or treat a spawned customer tool's sockets as a DR-105 component tail or as covered by host CA-4. Each result contradicts at least one recorded candidate and defeats the purpose of a phase-exact actor join.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Make the tail matrix typed and complete. State that the CA-1 SPAWN decision is the host head, while the admitted child component's egress is DR-105 / PT-NET-EGRESS and is not doctor CA-4. State separately that a CA-2 process-creation decision is host-side but the customer tool's later effects are neither admitted-component PT-NET-EGRESS nor host CA-4; CA-2 remains wholly unexercisable pending the recorded later product/authorization route. Explicitly surface the permission-v2/v6 CA-1/CA-2 recital as an inherited conflict that this candidate does not silently resolve.
